milwaukee-bicycle-collective-guide.label: Current shop, open hours and donation details

bike-new-york-guide.label: Recycle-A-Bicycle donation policy and Bike Lab drop-off

prep.label: Where to go
prep.text: Bring the donation during open shop hours. Check the home page for the current shop information.

prep.label: What may happen to the bike
prep.text: The collective describes repairing bikes, using them for parts or recycling when needed.

prep.label: Where to go
prep.text: Use the Bike Lab drop-off instructions and confirm current hours before arriving.

prep.label: Bikes needing repair
prep.text: The organizer may take damaged bikes or bikes missing parts. Disclose the condition before heading there.

prep.label: What to bring
prep.text: The shop lists adult and children's bikes in good to fair condition.

prep.label: When to arrive
prep.text: Use the shop's published hours and tell staff about major damage, rust or a bike missing most working parts.

prep.label: Where to go
prep.text: The donation page says its Bike Hubs can accept bikes, parts and tools. Confirm your chosen hub's current details before travel.

prep.label: How to leave the donation
prep.text: Hand it to the hub during open hours. The organizer asks people to avoid leaving donations outside.

tasks.label: Donate a bicycle with heavy rust
Have the shop pick up a bicycle

rules.text: The collective accepts bicycle donations during open shop hours.
The collective says it takes bicycles in any condition and explicitly discusses old rusty bikes.
The current shop page lists bicycle parts among the items it accepts.
The collective does not normally pick up bicycles. It may consider special arrangements case by case.
Bike New York welcomes bikes that work.
The donation policy excludes bicycles with excessive rust.
Bring usable parts. The shop excludes components that are beyond repair or excessively worn or rusty.
Bike New York lists new helmets only.
The Bike Lab occasionally offers local pickup for qualifying donations. Ask staff to confirm.
The shop accepts adult and children’s bikes in good to fair condition.
The shop says it can process severely rusty, damaged or mostly nonworking bikes with a suggested $10 donation per bike. Confirm the arrangement first.
The shop accepts new and used parts and tools in good condition.
The shop generally cannot pick up bikes. Ask if staff can consider a large group of bicycles.
The operator lists bicycle donations at its Bike Hubs.
The operator lists bike parts, accessories and tools for donation.
